neutral_facts.value: The accused, the wife of the deceased, was charged with abetment of suicide under Section 306 of the IPC. The deceased was found hanging in his home, and the mother of the deceased filed a complaint alleging harassment and abuse by the accused. The deceased had a child with the accused, and they had jointly purchased a house where they resided. The deceased was employed at a hospital. The complainant alleged that the accused harassed the deceased for money and to transfer the house into her name, sending vulgar messages and preventing the deceased from visiting his parents. Colleagues of the deceased also reported incidents of abuse. The accused claimed the deceased had a drinking problem and that the deceased may have committed suicide out of frustration. The police filed a chargesheet against the accused, but the trial court rejected her discharge application. The High Court dismissed the revision application, and the accused appealed to the Supreme Court.

quotes.text: Appellant is wife of deceased who committed suicide – Appellant and deceased resided in house jointly purchased by them – Cause of death ‘due to hanging’ – FIR lodged by mother of deceased under s. 306 IPC – Alleging deceased committed suicide because of harassment and beating by appellant on account of demand of money and for transfer of dwelling house in her name – Appellant allegedly also sent vulgar messages on mobile phone of deceased and would insist on him not visiting his parents and giving them money – Statement of colleague of deceased recorded wherein she referred to an incident when the appellant visited deceased and created a ruckus in the office by rushing towards him and being abusive – Chargesheet against appellant under section 306 of IPC – As per the chargesheet, offence took place at dwelling house where appellant harassed the deceased on account of money and for transfer of house in her name, inducing the deceased for attempt of suicide – Appellant preferred a discharge application before Trial Court – Trial Court rejected appellant’s discharge application – High Court dismissed the revision application against the Trial Court’s order.

quotes.text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

quotes.text: The Trial Court rejected the application. Aggrieved, the appellant preferred Criminal Revision Application before the High Court.
The High Court, by the impugned order, has dismissed the Revision and thus effectively dismissed the discharge application.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant-accused abetted the deceased's suicide through harassment, beating, and other acts, including sending vulgar messages and insisting the deceased not visit his parents, which led to the deceased's suicide.

quotes.text: The complaint was filed by Smt. Usha Gangurde, mother of deceased alleging physical and mental harassment by the accused.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no active role or positive act by the appellant to instigate or aid the deceased in committing suicide, and that the deceased may have committed suicide due to his own issues, such as alcohol addiction.

quotes.text: The counsel for Appellant that the deceased may have committed suicide out of frustration.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for a conviction under Section 306 IPC, there must be clear mens rea, an active or direct act leading the deceased to commit suicide, and a proximate link between the accused's conduct and the suicide.

quotes.text: Without a positive act on part of accused to instigate or aid in committing suicide, conviction cannot be sustained.
